$$\mathbb{E}[P(x)] = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\prod_{k=1}^{M}\left(x - \omega^{i_k}\right)\right] = \prod_{k=1}^{M} \mathbb{E}\!\left[x - \omega^{i_k}\right] = \prod_{k=1}^{M}\left(x - \mathbb{E}\!\left[\omega^{i_k}\right]\right)$$

Now compute $\mathbb{E}[\omega^{i_k}]$. Since $i_k$ is uniform on $\{0, \ldots, M-1\}$:

$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\omega^{i_k}\right] = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{j=0}^{M-1}\omega^j = \frac{1}{M}\cdot\frac{1 - \omega^M}{1 - \omega} = 0$$

$$\mathbb{E}[P(x)] = \prod_{k=1}^{M}(x - 0) = x^M \qquad (M \geq 2)$$
